chunks: Everything in this book that is narrated from Sa'd ibn Abdullah has been transmitted by me from my father, and from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan - may Allah be pleased with them both - from Sa'd ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Khalaf.

key_terms.أَبِي: My father, referring to Ali ibn Babawayh (Ali ibn al-Husayn), the father of the author.
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا: May Allah be pleased with them both, a phrase of respect used for the two narrators mentioned.
key_terms.سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Sa'd ibn Abdullah, a prominent companion of the Imams whose narrations are central to this text.
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْحَسَنِ: Muammad ibn al-Hasan, a key narrator in the chain of transmission.

ai.seo_question: Who are the narrators in the chain for Sa'd ibn Abdullah's hadiths in Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih?
ai.summary: This passage highlights the rigorous chain of transmission (isnad) in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih*, specifically linking the narrations of Sa'd ibn Abdullah to the author’s father and Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan. It underscores the scholarly emphasis on verifying the reliability of narrators to ensure the authenticity of the hadiths, a critical aspect of Shia hadith sciences. The mention of 'radiya Allahu 'anhuma' (may God be pleased with them) reflects the high esteem in which these key narrators are held within the Shia tradition.
